messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service `inference-runtime` (PD-987654). Severity: P1. Symptoms: sudden p99 latency spike across g4 pool, API error rate increased. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-987654

incident-bot: Recent counts: total_errors=412, 5xx_errors=238, p99_latency=2.3s, active_requests=1420

Jordan (sre-oncall): Acked. I'm on it — reassigning to on-call SRE and paging runtime. @Priya @Samir can you triage?

Priya (inference): ACK. Seeing a big uptick in KV cache misses and backend timeouts in traces. Likely cache invalidations -> model cold-starts. Querying metric buckets now.

Priya (inference): metrics snippet:
```
metric: inference.kv_cache_miss_count
window: 1m
now: 11.2k (baseline ~200)
hosts_affected: 6/18
```

Samir (runtime): Got it. Reproduced on staging with a synthetic load. A few pods hit OOM or blocked on kernel fallback, forcing slower path. Pulling logs from the hottest host now.

Samir (runtime): logs tail:
```
E 14:02:31 model_infer: kv_lookup_timeout 300ms host=10.2.3.45
W 14:02:32 allocator: fallback to float32 kernel for attention
Fatal 14:02:33 oom: process killed on pod inference-g4-7
```

Elena (support): FYI — Support thread: customer-redwood-payments reported timeouts on billing reconciliation (3 errors in last 2m). Marking severity high for external comms.

Jordan (sre-oncall): Quick mitigation plan: 1) Fail over a fraction of traffic to fallback region/model-variant, 2) Scale up replicas for affected pool, 3) Roll a kernel patch to avoid fallback on non-critical requests. I'm doing step 1 now to reduce customer impact.

Jordan (sre-oncall): Running routing change (canary):
```bash
# set route weight for model:open-instruct -> fallback-variant to 20%
redwoodctl routing set-weight --service inference-runtime --model open-instruct --variant fallback --weight 20
```

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: PD escalation to L2 requested. Notifying @Samir and @Priya for on-call takeover.

Samir (runtime): Acknowledged escalation. Starting a small rolling restart on 2 of 6 affected pods to clear corrupted caches. Will watch memory/latency.

Priya (inference): Autoscaler logs show scale events suppressed by sudden burst; minReplicas=2. Suggest bumping minReplicas to 6 for the pool to absorb spikes while we investigate.

Jordan (sre-oncall): Do it but watch cost. @Samir coordinate with infra to pre-warm containers to avoid cold-start penalty.

Samir (runtime): Increased minReplicas to 6 for g4-pool and requested pre-warm. Command run:
```
redwoodctl scale set --pool g4 --min 6 --target-cpu 65
```
Monitoring...

Elena (support): Drafting customer-facing status: "We are investigating intermittent timeouts affecting inference on a subset of requests. Engineers are mitigating and we will update in 30 minutes." Shall I post?

Jordan (sre-oncall): Yes post that now. Add note that some customers may see degraded throughput but no data loss.

Elena (support): Posted to status.redwood.com and notified affected accounts.

Samir (runtime): Latency trending down after restarts and routing canary. p99 now ~420ms (was 2.3s). Error rate dropping.

Priya (inference): KV miss count back to ~350/min. Looks like caches warmed back up after restarts + the canary.

Jordan (sre-oncall): Great. I'm going to close the active page in PD and create a follow-up ticket for root cause + permanent mitigations. Handoff: @Samir you'll own the follow-up (kernel fallback prevention + autoscaler tuning), @Priya to add regression tests for KV cache storm.

Samir (runtime): I’ll own the RCA and fix rollout. Tentative actions: patch to reduce fallback paths, increase memory headroom, test quantized kernels.

Jordan (sre-oncall): Closing PD-987654 as resolved. Thanks everyone. Please add any lingering notes to the follow-up ticket: INF-2345.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Incident PD-987654 marked RESOLVED by Jordan (sre-oncall) at 1876543365."
